sciMCH: Which simple machine is a doorknob?
Turning the large knob turns a small axle (shaft) that moves the latch.
Which simple machine is a chisel?
A chisel has a thin, sharp end that splits wood apart, so it is a wedge.
Which simple machine is a wheelchair ramp?
A ramp is a sloped surface that lets you raise a load with less force over a longer distance.
Which simple machine is the lid of a jar?
A jar lid has a spiral thread, which is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder: a screw.
Which simple machine is a hammer pulling out a nail?
The hammer pivots on its head, acting as a lever to pull the nail with less force.
Which simple machine is a sewing needle's point?
The sharp point of a needle is a wedge that pushes fabric fibres apart.
Which simple machine is a well bucket raised by a rope over a grooved wheel?
A rope running over a grooved wheel is a pulley, which changes the direction of the pull.
Which simple machine is a steering wheel?
A steering wheel is a large wheel attached to a smaller shaft (axle) that turns together with it.
Which simple machine is a light bulb's metal base?
The base of a bulb has a spiral thread that twists into the socket, so it is a screw.
Which simple machine is a bottle opener?
A bottle opener pivots on the edge of the cap and lifts it like a lever.
Which simple machine is a doorstop?
A doorstop is a wedge that jams into the gap under the door and holds it in place.
Which simple machine is a window blind's cord that runs over a small wheel?
The cord runs over a small wheel at the top of the blind, making it a pulley.
Which simple machine is a winding road up a mountain?
A road that slopes gradually up a mountain is a long inclined plane.
Which simple machine is a rolling pin?
A rolling pin's roller turns around a central rod, like a wheel and axle.
Which simple machine is a wheelbarrow's handles lifting a load?
The wheelbarrow pivots on its wheel, so lifting the handles works like a lever.
Which simple machine is a construction crane lifting steel with cables and wheels?
A crane lifts heavy loads using cables running over grooved wheels, which are pulleys.
Which simple machine is a drill bit?
A drill bit has spiral grooves wrapped around it, so it works like a screw.
Which simple machine is the front teeth you use to bite an apple?
Your front teeth are thin and sharp, so they act as wedges that split food apart.
Which simple machine is a loading ramp into a moving truck?
A loading ramp is a slope that lets people move heavy boxes up with less force.
Which simple machine is a pencil sharpener's turning handle?
The crank handle turns in a big circle that spins a small axle inside, like a wheel and axle.
Which simple machine is a canoe paddle pushing water?
A paddle pivots in your hands, acting as a lever to push against the water.
Which simple machine is a stool's twisting height adjuster?
A threaded post that twists to raise or lower the seat is a screw.

Balanced forces, so it stays still

Unbalanced forces, so it speeds up
Unbalanced forces, so it slows down
Unbalanced forces, so it changes direction

Balanced forces, so its motion does not change
Unbalanced forces, so it speeds up
Unbalanced forces, so it slows down

Balanced forces, so it stays still

Balanced forces, so it stays still
Balanced forces, so its motion does not change

Balanced forces, so it stays still

Unbalanced forces, so it speeds up

Unbalanced forces, so it speeds up

Unbalanced forces, so its motion changes
Balanced forces, so it stays still
Balanced forces, so its motion does not change

Unbalanced forces, so it changes direction

Unbalanced forces, so its motion changes
Balanced forces, so it stays still

No forces act on it at all

Balanced forces, so its motion does not change
Unbalanced forces, so it speeds up

Unbalanced forces, so its motion changes
Balanced forces, so it stays still

Balanced forces, so its motion does not change
Unbalanced forces, so it speeds up
Unbalanced forces, so it slows down
Unbalanced forces, so it changes direction

Unbalanced forces, so its motion changes
Balanced forces, so it stays still

sciMassForce: A force of 10 N gives a cart an acceleration of 2 m/s². What happens if the cart's mass is cut in half and the force stays 10 N?
Acceleration is force divided by mass, so halving the mass doubles the acceleration.
Which needs the greatest force to reach the same acceleration?
With the same acceleration, the object with the most mass needs the most force.
What force is needed to accelerate a 5 kg box at 2 m/s²?
Force equals mass times acceleration: 5 kg × 2 m/s² = 10 N.
A 2 kg ball is pushed with 8 N of force. What is its acceleration?
Acceleration equals force divided by mass: 8 N ÷ 2 kg = 4 m/s².
Two wagons are pulled with the same force. Wagon A has a mass of 20 kg and wagon B has 40 kg. Which statement is true?
Wagon A accelerates twice as much as wagon B
Wagon B accelerates twice as much as wagon A
Both wagons accelerate the same amount
With equal force, half the mass gives twice the acceleration.
If both the force and the mass are doubled, the acceleration …
Acceleration is force ÷ mass, so doubling both leaves the ratio unchanged.
Why is it harder to start pushing a full shopping cart than an empty one?
The full cart has more mass, so it needs more force to accelerate
The full cart has less friction
The empty cart has more inertia
Gravity does not act on empty carts
More mass means more force is needed to produce the same acceleration.
A hockey player hits a puck and a tennis ball with the same force. Which speeds up more? (The puck has more mass.)
They speed up the same amount
With the same force, the object with less mass gets the greater acceleration.
What is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its motion called?
Inertia is an object's resistance to changes in motion, and it increases with mass.
Which object has the most inertia?
A pickup truck with nothing in it
Inertia depends on mass, and the loaded transport truck has the greatest mass.
If you push three times as hard on the same sled, its acceleration …
Acceleration is directly proportional to force when mass stays the same.
A 50 N force accelerates a wagon at 5 m/s². What is the wagon's mass?
Mass equals force divided by acceleration: 50 N ÷ 5 m/s² = 10 kg.
Which equation links force, mass and acceleration?
Newton's second law says force equals mass times acceleration.
A rocket burns fuel and gets lighter while its engine force stays the same. What happens to its acceleration?
With the same force and less mass, the acceleration increases.
Why do heavy trucks need bigger brakes than small cars?
More mass needs more force to slow it down
To produce the same deceleration, a larger mass requires a larger force.
An empty canoe and a canoe full of gear are paddled with the same force. Which speeds up faster?
The empty canoe has less mass, so the same force gives it more acceleration.
A 3 kg rock and a 6 kg rock are each given an acceleration of 2 m/s². How much force does the 6 kg rock need compared with the 3 kg rock?
At the same acceleration, force is proportional to mass, and 6 kg is twice 3 kg.
What is the unit of force?
Force is measured in newtons, where 1 N accelerates 1 kg at 1 m/s².
A bowling ball and a beach ball are rolling at the same speed. Which needs more force to stop in the same time?
The bowling ball has more mass, so more force is needed to change its motion in the same time.
A force of 12 N acts on a 4 kg object. What is the acceleration?
Acceleration equals force divided by mass: 12 N ÷ 4 kg = 3 m/s².
Why does a sprinter want light running shoes?
Less mass lets the same leg force produce more acceleration
Light shoes increase gravity on the runner
Reducing mass means the same force gives a greater acceleration.
You throw a baseball and a shot put with the same force. Which statement is correct?
The baseball accelerates more because it has less mass
The shot put accelerates more because it has more mass
Both accelerate equally because the force is the same
Neither accelerates because they are thrown
For a given force, a smaller mass produces a larger acceleration.
sciLifeCyc: Which animal goes through complete metamorphosis?
Ladybugs go from egg to larva to pupa to adult, which is complete metamorphosis.
Which animal goes through incomplete metamorphosis?
Crickets hatch as nymphs that look like small adults and moult until grown, which is incomplete metamorphosis.
Which animal has no metamorphosis and is born looking like a small adult?
A foal looks like a small horse and simply grows bigger, so there is no metamorphosis.
What are the four stages of complete metamorphosis, in order?
In complete metamorphosis, an insect hatches as a larva, rests as a pupa and emerges as an adult.
What are the three stages of incomplete metamorphosis?
Incomplete metamorphosis skips the pupa stage: egg, nymph, then adult.
What is a young grasshopper called?
Insects with incomplete metamorphosis, like grasshoppers, hatch as nymphs.
The larva stage of a butterfly or moth
The pupa stage of a butterfly
An adult insect with no wings
A caterpillar is the eating and growing larva stage of a butterfly or moth.
A frog changes from a tadpole with gills to an adult with lungs. What is this change called?
A big change in body form during the life cycle, like tadpole to frog, is metamorphosis.
Which stage is missing in incomplete metamorphosis?
Insects with incomplete metamorphosis never form a pupa; the nymph moults directly into an adult.
How is a frog's life cycle different from a bird's?
A frog changes form from tadpole to adult, but a bird does not
A bird changes form from tadpole to adult, but a frog does not
Frogs give birth to live young but birds lay eggs
Birds have a pupa stage but frogs do not
Frogs go through metamorphosis, while baby birds hatch looking like small versions of adults.
A larva changes into an adult butterfly
An adult turns back into a caterpillar
The chrysalis is the pupa stage, where the body is rebuilt into the adult form.
Which animal has a life cycle most like a mosquito's?
Mosquitoes and houseflies both go through complete metamorphosis: egg, larva, pupa, adult.
Which animal has a life cycle most like a cockroach's?
Cockroaches and praying mantises both go through incomplete metamorphosis with nymphs.
What kind of life cycle does a salamander have?
Metamorphosis from a water-breathing larva to an adult
Live birth with no change in body form
Like frogs, salamanders are amphibians that hatch as gilled larvae and change into adults.
How does a young mammal usually start its life?
It is born alive and drinks milk from its mother
It hatches as a larva and forms a pupa
It hatches as a nymph and moults
It starts as a tadpole in water
Most mammals give birth to live young that feed on their mother's milk.
Why does a nymph moult several times?
Its hard outer skeleton cannot grow, so it sheds it to get bigger
Insects have a stiff exoskeleton, so they must shed it to grow larger.
A young honeybee is a legless grub in a wax cell. Which stage is this?
A legless, worm-like young insect that eats and grows is a larva.
Which stage of a monarch butterfly mainly eats milkweed leaves?
Monarch caterpillars feed on milkweed leaves to grow before forming a chrysalis.
Which pair of animals both have no metamorphosis?
Snakes and robins both hatch looking like small adults and simply grow.
How does a young dragonfly nymph live?
Inside a cocoon on a tree
In a nest fed by its parents
As a pupa in the soil
Dragonfly nymphs live in ponds and streams and breathe with gills until they become flying adults.
In which life cycle does the young look most different from the adult?
In complete metamorphosis the larva, such as a caterpillar or maggot, looks nothing like the adult.
Which statement about a chicken's life cycle is true?
A chick hatches from an egg and grows into an adult without changing form
A chick hatches as a larva and forms a pupa
A chick hatches as a nymph and moults its skin
A chicken gives birth to live chicks
Chickens have no metamorphosis; a chick is a small version of the adult bird.
sciXsPlFood: What gas do plants take in from the air to make food?
Plants take in carbon dioxide through their leaves and use it in photosynthesis.
What energy source do plants use to make food?
Plants capture the energy of sunlight to make sugar.
Which part of a plant carries water up from the roots to the leaves?
The stem has tubes that carry water from the roots up to the leaves.
Chlorophyll is a green substance that absorbs light for photosynthesis.
Why are leaves often wide and flat?
A wide, flat surface catches more sunlight for making food.
Besides water, what do roots take in from the soil?
Roots absorb water and minerals that help the plant grow.
Which of these is stored food from a plant that people eat?
A potato is an underground stem that stores food the plant made.
Maple syrup is made from maple sap. Where did the sugar in the sap come from?
Food the tree made in its leaves
Sugar the tree took from the soil

Which is a good place for a houseplant to make lots of food?

Plants make food from sunlight, and animals cannot

Gives it all back to the soil
Plants use sugar for energy and to build new leaves, stems and roots.

It has too much carbon dioxide
Without light, the plant cannot photosynthesize and loses its green colour.
Which part of a carrot plant do we eat, where food is stored?
A carrot is a root that stores food for the plant.
What do plants release into the air that animals need to breathe?

Which three things does a plant need to make food?
Photosynthesis uses light energy, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar.

To make the seed heavier for the soil

Which word means "making food using light"?

A cactus's leaves are spines, so its green stem carries out photosynthesis.

There is no air in a forest
The soil has too much water
With less light, plants on the forest floor make less food and grow slowly.
Where in a plant cell does photosynthesis happen?
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are where light is used to make sugar.
What happens to a plant that gets light and air but no water?
It wilts and cannot make food
Water is needed for photosynthesis, so without it the plant wilts and cannot make food.

It carries pollen to other flowers while drinking nectar.
It buries the flower's seeds underground.
It blows the petals to new places.
It eats the flower's leaves.

Bees carry the seeds on their legs.
The seeds stick to animal fur.
Squirrels drop the seeds into rivers.

Planting seeds in soil.
Watering a plant's roots.
Dropping leaves in autumn.
Pollination moves pollen so a flower can make seeds.

It sticks to animal fur.
Wind blows it high into the air.
Coconuts have a light, air-filled husk that lets them float to new beaches.
Why do flowers make sweet nectar?

To keep the roots warm.
To make the seeds heavier.
To scare away the wind.
Nectar attracts pollinators, which carry pollen as they move between flowers.
Which animal is a pollinator?

An earthworm
A snail
A trout
Butterflies drink nectar and carry pollen between flowers.

A bee collecting nectar
A spider spinning a web
A frog catching flies
Robins eat berries and drop the seeds in their droppings in new places.
How do some seeds travel by sticking to your socks?

They are sticky with nectar.
They have wings that grab the socks.
They float in the air until they land on socks.
Hooked seeds like burdock grab onto fur and clothing and are carried away.

So the seeds stay in the shade.

How are grass flowers usually pollinated?
By the wind
By hummingbirds
By bats
By butterflies
Grasses have small, plain flowers that release light pollen into the wind.
Why do wind-pollinated flowers usually not have bright petals or a scent?
They do not need to attract animals.
They want to hide from the wind.
Bright petals would make the pollen heavy.
They grow only at night.
Since wind carries their pollen, these plants do not spend energy attracting pollinators.
How does a pea pod spread its seeds?
The dry pod bursts open and flings the seeds out.
The seeds float down rivers.
Bees carry the seeds away.
The seeds have hooks that catch on fur.
Some pods dry and twist until they snap open, throwing the seeds away from the plant.
What would happen to apple trees if there were no bees?
Many flowers would not be pollinated, so fewer apples would grow.
The trees would grow more apples.
The apples would grow without flowers.
The trees would grow taller instead.
Apple flowers need pollinators like bees to make fruit and seeds.
Why does a strawberry have a sweet, red fruit?
To attract animals that eat it and spread the seeds.
To attract the wind.
To keep the plant warm.
To stop animals from finding it.
Tasty, colourful fruit gets animals to eat it and carry the seeds elsewhere.
What part of a flower makes pollen?
The stamen
The root
The leaf
The stem
Pollen is made in the anther, at the top of the stamen.
Which of these is a seed disperser?
A chipmunk that stores seeds
A moth drinking nectar
A bee buzzing in a flower
A ladybug eating aphids
Chipmunks carry and bury seeds, and some of the seeds grow into plants.
How does a cattail spread its seeds?
Fluffy seeds are carried by the wind.
Seeds roll down hills.
Bees carry the seeds.
Seeds are thrown by exploding pods.
Cattail seeds have fluffy hairs that let them drift on the wind.
A moth visits pale flowers that smell strongest at night. What does this tell you?
The flowers are adapted to be pollinated by night animals.
The flowers are pollinated by the wind.
The flowers do not make pollen.
The flowers make seeds without pollination.
Pale colours and night-time scent help moths find the flowers in the dark.
How does a water lily's seed often spread?
It floats on the water to a new spot.
It sticks to bird feathers in flight.
It is flung by a bursting pod.
Bees carry it to the shore.
Water lily seeds can float for a while before sinking to grow in a new spot.
sciBiome: Which ecosystem is described? Cone-bearing evergreen trees, long cold winters, moose and lynx.
The boreal (taiga) forest has conifers, cold winters and animals like moose and lynx.
Which ecosystem is described? Shallow standing water, cattails, frogs and ducks.
Wetlands such as marshes are covered by shallow water and full of cattails, frogs and waterbirds.
Which ecosystem is described? Flowing fresh water, trout and smooth stones on the bottom.
A river is a freshwater ecosystem of moving water where fish like trout live.
Which ecosystem is described? Treeless land in the far north, Arctic foxes, snowy owls and lichens.
The tundra is cold and treeless, with lichens and animals like Arctic foxes.
Which ecosystem is described? Prairie grasses, hot summers, cold winters and gophers digging burrows.
Canada's prairies are grasslands with few trees and burrowing animals like gophers.
Which ecosystem is described? Warm, shallow salt water with colourful corals and many fish.
Coral reefs form in warm, shallow ocean water and are home to many fish.
Which ecosystem is described? Maple, oak and beech trees with bright colours in autumn.
Deciduous trees like maples and oaks change colour and drop their leaves in autumn.
Which ecosystem is described? Sandy dunes, camels, and only a few centimetres of rain a year.
Deserts get very little rain and have animals adapted to dry conditions, like camels.
Which ecosystem is described? Small, still body of fresh water with lily pads, tadpoles and dragonflies.
A pond is a small freshwater ecosystem with still water and plants like lily pads.
Which ecosystem is described? Jaguars, sloths and vines climbing toward the sunlight under heavy rain.
Tropical rainforests are hot and rainy, with vines, sloths and jaguars.
Which ecosystem is described? Deep, dark, cold salt water where fish make their own light.
In the deep ocean, no sunlight reaches, so some fish glow to find food or mates.
Which ecosystem is described? Huge open plains with tall grass, lions and herds of zebras and giraffes.
A savanna is a tropical grassland with scattered trees and large grazing animals.
Which ecosystem is described? Spruce, fir and pine trees, deep winter snow and black bears.
Spruce, fir and pine are typical conifers of the boreal forest.
Which ecosystem is described? Muskoxen, permafrost and tiny flowers that bloom in a short summer.
Muskoxen live on the tundra, where plants grow quickly in a short summer.
Which ecosystem is described? Salty water, kelp forests, sea otters and sea urchins.
Kelp forests grow in the ocean, where sea otters eat sea urchins.
Which ecosystem is described? Spongy ground, sphagnum moss and acidic water.
A bog is a wetland with wet, acidic soil covered in sphagnum moss.
Which ecosystem is described? Hot sand, Joshua trees, rattlesnakes and very dry air.
Rattlesnakes and Joshua trees are adapted to hot, dry desert conditions.
Which ecosystem is described? Poison dart frogs, orchids and a canopy of tall trees in steady rain.
Poison dart frogs and orchids live in warm, wet tropical rainforests.
Which ecosystem is described? Ice-covered sea, polar bears hunting seals on floating ice.
Polar bears hunt seals from the sea ice of the Arctic Ocean.
Which ecosystem is described? White-tailed deer, chipmunks and a thick layer of fallen leaves on the forest floor.
Each autumn, deciduous trees drop leaves that cover the forest floor.
Which ecosystem is described? Bison grazing on wide plains of grass with very few trees.
Bison are grazing animals that live on open grasslands.
Which ecosystem is described? Fresh water meeting salt water where a river flows into the sea.
An estuary is where fresh river water mixes with salty ocean water.
sciXsEco: Which is an abiotic (non-living) factor in a desert ecosystem?
Sand
Cactus
Lizard
Scorpion
Sand is not alive, so it is an abiotic factor.
Which is a biotic (living) factor in a pond ecosystem?
Algae
Sunlight
Mud
Water temperature
Algae are living things, so they are biotic factors.
What do we call a group of the same species living in one area?
A population
A community
An ecosystem
A biome
A population is all the members of one species living in the same place.
What is a habitat?
The place where an organism lives and gets what it needs
The food an animal eats to get its energy
A group of different species living together
